source: A baseline output (bench/shape/runs/baseline/planted-shared-parser.1), hand-graded by the building thread after reading it against the case's seed repo.

issue.title: csv2json: add a --tsv flag to read tab-separated input
issue.problem: bin/csv2json.js ignores its command-line arguments and always calls parse(readFileSync(0,'utf8')) with the default comma separator, so tab-separated input comes out as one column per line (e.g. printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js prints [{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]). The shared parser in src/parse.js already accepts a separator argument (parse(text, sep = ',')), but the CLI exposes no way to choose it. README.md documents only CSV usage.
issue.reason: Users' exports now arrive as TSV and they must pre-convert them with sed before running csv2json; a sed tab-to-comma rewrite also corrupts any field that contains a comma.
issue.outcome: Running node bin/csv2json.js --tsv on tab-separated stdin prints the same JSON array of header-keyed objects that CSV input produces, while CSV behaviour without the flag and the exported parse() function stay exactly as they are.
expect: printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv prints exactly [{"a":"1","b":"2"}] followed by a newline and exits 0.
With --tsv, commas inside a field are kept as data: printf 'a\tb\nx,y\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv prints exactly [{"a":"x,y","b":"2"}] followed by a newline.
With --tsv, CRLF line endings are handled: printf 'a\tb\r\n1\t2\r\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv prints exactly [{"a":"1","b":"2"}] followed by a newline.

Without --tsv, CSV behaviour is unchanged: printf 'a,b
1,2
' | node bin/csv2json.js prints exactly [{"a":"1","b":"2"}] followed by a newline, and printf 'a	b,c
1	2,3
' | node bin/csv2json.js prints exactly [{"a	b":"1	2","c":"3"}] followed by a newline (tabs are not treated as separators by default).

The exported parse in src/parse.js keeps its comma default and separator argument: node -e "import('./src/parse.js').then(m=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(m.parse('a,b
1,2
')));console.log(JSON.stringify(m.parse('a	b
1	2
','	')))})" prints [{"a":"1","b":"2"}] on both lines.
npm test passes, and test/csv.test.js contains a test that runs bin/csv2json.js with the --tsv argument on tab-separated input and asserts its JSON output.
README.md documents the --tsv flag with a usage example.

non_goals: Quoted fields, escaped separators, or full RFC 4180 / TSV escaping support.
Auto-detecting the delimiter, or a general --delimiter/--sep option.
Changing the default (no-flag) CSV behaviour or the JSON output format.
Publishing a new npm release or bumping the package version.
assumptions: The flag is spelled exactly --tsv and only switches the input separator to a tab; the output stays the same JSON array.
Input still comes from stdin as today; no file-path argument is added.
Behaviour for unknown flags is left unspecified by this issue.
Reusing the existing separator parameter of parse() in src/parse.js is the suggested approach but not required, as long as parse()'s exported behaviour is unchanged.
